text.p: Base metals eased their grip on recent gains on Wednesday as prices eroded in lacklustre trade.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 2.06 points lower at 243.76.

Three months copper drifted lower throughout the day and finished the kerb at the day's lows of $2,375, down $20 from the previous close. It had started strong above $2,400, thanks in part to news that Asarco's copper output in southern Peru had been curtailed due to flooding.

Aluminium similarly crumbled below important nearby support at $1,680 and settled at $1,673, a decline of $13. Dampening sentiment was news that Russian producers revised up the country's primary aluminium exports for 1996 to 2.44 million tonnes, from 2.37 million tonnes previously.
Zinc settled $10 lower to $1,240, the level which earlier this week had heralded the metal's rise to 4-1/2 year highs.

Lead sank sharply as market makers unwound their hedges for the key $625 call options, traders noted. Prices posted a decline of $18, settling at $680. Analysts said the $675/$680 area was important support which if breached would target $665, analysts said.
Nickel traded in a relatively narrow range following Tuesday's sharp losses and ended the kerb just $20 easier at $8,080.
Tin was also little changed at $5,835, down $25, while alloy was last quoted at $1,553/55, compared to $1,555 on Tuesday.

CBOT wheat futures were mixed at midsession with May and July firm on concerns some soft red winter wheat may be damaged by flooding this week in the U.S. Ohio River Valley, traders said. At 1112 CST, soft red winter wheat futures were 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with March down 1-1/2 at $3.69-1/2.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures slid further late morning Wednesday, as funds turned gold sellers again after the month-long recovery ran out of steam earlier this week, traders said. "Gold had already been down for the past two days, so the Swiss news today was just the straw that broke the camel's back," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said. In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $352.25/75, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $354.50 and the New York close Tuesday at $358.60/359.10.

CSCE world sugar futures were weaker at midsession on local liquidation and speculative selling, market sources said. A broker said early trade buying out of the Far East lifted the benchmark May contract to the top of the trading range at 10.95 cents a lb. At 1130 EST, CSCE May sugar was down 0.10 cent at 10.78 cents, traded 10.95 to 10.76 cents a lb. Deferreds were 0.09 to 0.05 cent weaker.

NYMEX crude oil prices had given back its gains by midday Wednesday after starting off higher in the wake of bullish inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute and the Energy Information Adminintration. At 1225 EST/1725 GMT, April crude stood nine cents lower at $20.57 a barrel, with further downward moves predicted.
